title: Ops sync cheatsheet + SLO deep-dive prep (weekly)
content:
Purpose: quick reference and talking points for this week's SRE ops sync / reliability review. Use this to run the 30–45m meeting; keep it tight.

Meeting info
- Time: weekly ops sync (Thu 10:00–10:45 PT) — bring SLO owners and one oncall rep.
- Objective: surface any regression in SLOs, review paging trends, triage top incidents, agree on action items for the week.
- Prep ask (send by EOD Wed): SLO owner must paste one-line status and any blocking work.

Agenda (30–45m)
1) Quick SLO health snapshot (5–8m) — runbook owner leads
   - p50/p95/p99 error budget burn, highlight any SLOs < 90% of target
   - callouts: recent config changes that might affect metrics (caching, routing)
2) Paging trends + meta (8–10m) — oncall summary
   - weekly page counts by service, % repeat pages, time-of-day peaks
   - top 3 recurring page reasons (eg auth timeouts, model spinup failures, infra OOMs)
3) Incident highlights (10–12m) — each incident owner gives 2-min summary
   - INC-2026-048 (cache-eviction spike) — brief RCA status and next steps
   - INC-2026-053 (model-quantization fallback loop) — is rollback scheduled?
4) Action items + owners (5–10m) — confirm who picks up what, due dates, and follow-ups
5) AOB (if time): upcoming infra maintenance windows, Dedicated capacity changes, support escalations

SLO health summary (quick bullets to paste into meeting)\- API request success SLO (99.5% target): 99.63% last 7d, but 98.8% during Tue 03:00–05:00 incident window — watch for regression if p99 latency climbs next week.
- Chat generation latency SLO (p95 < 350ms): 92% met last 7d, sliding downside trend from 96% two weeks ago. Likely related to increased burst from shared-hosted pool.
- Embedding throughput SLO (99% availability): stable at 99.9%.

Paging trends (ops notes)
- Total pages last week: 48 (avg 6.8/day). Up 22% vs prior week.
- Repeat pages (same problem reopened within 72h): 28% (we want <20%).
- Peak window: 02:00–05:00 PT (automated maintenance + region failover noise).
- Top page reasons: 1) cache eviction cascade (INC-2026-048) 2) model cold-start timeouts on smaller instances 3) RBAC token rotation flaps.

Incidents to call out (short, actionable)
- INC-2026-048 — cache-eviction spike (Tue 2026-05-05 02:10–03:50)\  Owner: Diego Ramos.\  Status: RCA draft, root cause likely mis-sized LRU window after a deploy to Dedicated pool.\  Immediate mitigation: raised cache size and throttled prefix write burst.\  Next: permanent tuning + add alert on eviction-rate > X (owner: Diego, due 2026-05-17).
- INC-2026-053 — quantization fallback loop (Wed 2026-05-06)\  Owner: Aisha Khan.\  Status: mitigated via hotfix revert; postmortem in progress.\  Next: add CI model-variant compatibility test + gating for rollout (owner: Aisha, due 2026-05-24).
- Minor: region-network flaps in eu-west-2 caused 3 degraded requests — follow-up: network team to share maintenance schedule with SRE (action: JM, due 2026-05-12).

Suggested metrics/queries to run live in sync\- Datadog: avg(last_1h):max:service.request.errors{env:prod} by {service} 
- Datadog: sum:service.pages.count{reason:cache_eviction}.rollup(sum, 3600)
- Kibana: search "timed out waiting for kv cache" since -24h for hostgroup ro-*/
- Console: /console/slo?team=sre&window=7d (paste current SLO table)

Open questions to surface\- Is the latency regression for chat tied to recent autoscaler changes in hosted pool? (ask infra autoscaler owners)\- Should we raise a stronger paging threshold for eviction-related alerts to reduce noise?\- Are there outstanding backlog items from last month's reliability retro that still need owners assigned?

Action items (capture during meeting)
- Diego: finalize cache eviction RCA and create tuning PR, add eviction-rate alert (due 2026-05-17).
- Aisha: finish postmortem for quantization fallback, add CI gating ticket (JIRA: INFRA-1127) (due 2026-05-24).
- JM (network): confirm maintenance calendar for eu-west-2 and propose quieter window (due 2026-05-12).
- SLO owners: paste one-line status + two risks to Slack #sre-ops by Wed EOD.
- Oncall lead: schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to validate eviction-rate alert behavior (owner: oncall lead, due 2026-05-19).

Quick links for the meeting\- SLO dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/slo\- Pager analytics (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/pager-ops\- RCA template (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/RCA+Template

Notes to self (things to say)\- Keep the sync to 30m: if technical deep-dive is needed, create a follow-up.\- Push for concrete due dates and owners on the spot.\- Highlight the repeat page metric — it's the best predictor of churn.

Post-meeting follow-up template (paste into Slack after meeting)
"TL;DR from ops sync: 3 action items assigned (Diego, Aisha, JM). Summary: cache-eviction RCA, quantization postmortem, network maintenance calendar. Next check-in: follow-up on eviction alert on 2026-05-19. Full notes + links: <link to doc>"

Misc scratch bits (commands & quick checks)\- Check eviction rate: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://infra-api.internal/v1/metrics?metric=cache_eviction_rate&window=1h" | jq .\- Quick log tail for model fallback: kubectl -n hosted logs deploy/model-router --since=2h | grep quantize

End of page — leave this doc as single-source scratch for the meeting. Move finalized meeting notes to Confluence / SRE weekly folder after sync.
